0.1.n: A place name, used here as part of the name 江戸幕府.

0.2.n: Refers to the military government headed by a shogun.

0.3.n: Links 江戸幕府 to its first shogun.

0.4.n: Specifies the first person to hold the position.

0.5.n: A title for Japan’s military ruler under this system.

0.6.n: Marks the first shogun as the topic of the question.

0.7.n: Asks for the identity of the person holding that position.

0.8.n: Part of でしょう, which makes this a polite quiz-style question.

0.9.n: Completes でしょう; this subtitle split does not give う a separate meaning.

0.12.n: Marks the preceding question as the words someone asks.

0.13.n: 聞く becomes passive 聞かれる, then conditional 聞かれたら, describing what happens if someone is asked.

0.15.n: Used with の before 人 to describe a large number of people.

0.16.n: Connects 多く to 人, forming 多くの人.

0.17.n: Japanese nouns do not need a plural ending; 多く makes the plural sense clear.

0.18.n: Marks 多くの人 as those who can answer.

0.19.n: The ability form of 答える, not a passive form here.

0.20.n: Marks the preceding statement as what the speaker thinks.

0.21.n: The polite form of 思う; the speaker is understood without saying 私.

1.0.n: The family name of Tokugawa Ieyasu; Japanese names normally put the family name first.

1.1.n: The personal name of Tokugawa Ieyasu, the first shogun of the Edo shogunate.

1.2.n: Politely identifies the answer; the subject is omitted because it is clear.

2.0.n: The family name of Oda Nobunaga, a historical military leader.

2.1.n: The personal name of Oda Nobunaga.

2.3.n: The family name of Toyotomi Hideyoshi, a historical ruler.

2.4.n: The personal name of Toyotomi Hideyoshi.

2.5.n: Marks Nobunaga and Hideyoshi as the people Ieyasu ranks beside.

2.6.n: Literally describes lining up, but here compares historical fame.

2.7.n: Shows the degree of fame: enough to rank alongside those two figures.

2.8.n: Describes Ieyasu and needs な when placed directly before his name.

2.9.n: Connects 有名 to the following name so it describes that person.

2.10.n: The family name of Tokugawa Ieyasu.

2.11.n: The personal name of the historical figure being introduced.

2.12.n: Gives the introduction a polite ending before が connects it to what follows.

2.13.n: Connects this introduction to the next point, suggesting a contrast.

3.0.n: A historical term for someone who holds supreme power over the country.

3.1.n: Marks the position reached with なる; となる is a more formal alternative to になる.

3.2.n: The past form of なる, placed before 秀吉 to describe him.

3.3.n: Toyotomi Hideyoshi’s personal name, used without his family name here.

3.4.n: Marks Hideyoshi as the person who was wary.

3.5.n: Oda Nobunaga’s personal name, used without his family name here.

3.7.n: Refers to later generations of Nobunaga’s family.

3.8.n: Marks the descendants as the people Hideyoshi regarded with caution.

3.9.n: 警戒する becomes past 警戒した, presenting Hideyoshi’s caution as a past fact.

3.10.n: Forms ように with the next word to compare Hideyoshi’s behavior with Ieyasu’s.

3.11.n: Completes ように, making the preceding situation a comparison for the next clause.

4.0.n: Repeats the historical title to show that Ieyasu reached the same position as Hideyoshi.

4.1.n: Marks the resulting position in the expression となる.

4.2.n: The past form of なる, placed before 家康 to describe him.

4.3.n: Tokugawa Ieyasu’s personal name, used without his family name here.

4.4.n: Adds Ieyasu to the comparison: he showed the same caution as Hideyoshi.

4.5.n: Toyotomi Hideyoshi’s personal name; his descendants are now the focus of concern.

4.7.n: Refers to later generations of Hideyoshi’s family.

4.8.n: Marks the descendants as the people Ieyasu was wary of.

4.9.n: 警戒する uses polite ています to describe continuing caution; this historical narration concerns the past.

0.lit: If asked, Who might the Edo shogunate’s first shogun be?, I think many people can answer.
0.tip: 答えられる expresses ability here: people can answer, rather than people being answered.

1.tip: Japanese puts family names first: 徳川 is the family name, and 家康 is the personal name.

2.lit: It is Tokugawa Ieyasu, famous enough to rank alongside Oda Nobunaga and Toyotomi Hideyoshi, but…
2.tip: A verb followed by ほど gives a degree: 並ぶほど有名 means famous enough to rank alongside them.

3.lit: Just as Hideyoshi, who became ruler of the realm, was wary of Nobunaga’s descendants,
3.tip: ように after a clause means just as, setting up a comparison with the following line.

4.lit: Ieyasu, who became ruler of the realm, also is wary of Hideyoshi’s descendants.
4.tip: Although 警戒しています has a present-style ending, this historical narration describes Ieyasu’s continuing caution in the past.
